name: What is the difference between dry-stacked and mortared stone installation?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between dry-stacked and mortared stone installation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dry-stacked stone installation involves carefully fitting stones together without mortar, relying on gravity, friction, and the stone's natural shape for stability. This method often creates a rustic, permeable aesthetic, ideal for garden walls or natural-looking features. Mortared installation, conversely, uses a cement-based mixture to bind stones together, creating a more rigid, durable, and less permeable structure. Mortared applications are common for load-bearing walls, patios, and outdoor fireplaces, offering greater structural integrity and a more refined finish.
acceptedAnswer.description: Dry-stacked stone uses no mortar, relying on stone fit for a rustic, permeable look. Mortared stone uses cement to bind, creating a rigid, durable, and less permeable structure for load-bearing or refined features.
